text:
maya: Terraform plan blocked by Conftest/OPA in staging when trying to create a small NV6 GPU pool. Getting an egress/egress-rule violation and a tag requirement. Need an emergency-ish approval during the maintenance freeze window.

ops-bot: POLICY CHECK FAILED: conftest (policy: required-tags, network:egress) - https://ci.redwood.example/policy/12345 - run `conftest test` locally to reproduce.

maya: plan snippet: ```
# module.gpu_pool.google_compute_instance_group.manager
+ resource "google_compute_instance_group_manager" "gpu_manager" {
+   name               = "nv6-canary-igm"
+   base_instance_name = "nv6-canary"
+   target_size        = 2
+ }

# google_compute_firewall.egress-allow
+ resource "google_compute_firewall" "egress-allow" {
+   network = "projects/redwood/global/networks/private-net"
+   allows  = [{ protocol = "tcp", ports = ["443"] }]
+ }
```

sam: quick q — what's the risk if we delay? is this for an experiment or customer traffic?

jordan: it's for a canary internal workload to validate a new batching config. low traffic, but we need GPUs to repro performance regressions. we could use preemptible NV4s but those give noisy perf.

lee: FYI quota in us-west2 for nv6 is nearly exhausted (only 4 free). If you create 2 more instances that could push us over for other teams. Suggest creating a canary pool in us-east1 instead, or reduce target_size to 1.

maya: can we get a time-limited exception for the policy failures? Conftest is flagging missing `owner` and `sla_tier` tags plus an egress rule that references an external CIDR instead of the approved egress-proxy. I can add tags quickly. The egress rule is needed for metrics ingestion to our SaaS provider.

sam: if you can push a quick PR with the tags and change the firewall to use `egress-proxy.redwood.internal` we can re-run plan. If the change still fails policy, we can route the request to @eng-infra-policy for a manual waiver.

maya: putting the PR link: https://github.com/redwood-infra/terraform/compare/evg/nv6-canary-tags - includes `tags = { owner = "maya", sla_tier = "canary" }` and replaces CIDR with approved DNS host in a NAT rule.

ops-bot: Policy waiver required: freeze-window block active (freeze: 2026-11-01T22:00:00Z -> 2026-11-02T06:00:00Z). Exemptions must include justification and TTL. Open an exemption ticket: https://infra.redwood.example/exemptions/new

jordan: Suggested exemption text: "Short-lived canary for batching perf validation; 1-hour TTL; risk: limited to internal monitoring only; fallback: immediate scale-down and detach if noisy." Sam, can you +1 to move to policy channel?

sam: +1. Also note: include capacity mitigation (will run in us-east1) and cost estimate (~$12/hr during test).

lee: @maya if you still want us-west2, I can temporarily bump project quota by 2 after approval, but prefer us-east1 to avoid impacting customers.

maya: updated the PR to set target_size = 1 and added tags. Retrying plan now.

ops-bot: CONFTST RESULT: PASSED (required-tags), FAILED (network:egress). See log: https://ci.redwood.example/conftest/67890

jordan: For the egress policy, you can add a short-lived firewall that uses a host-based NAT via approved proxy, or add `egress: { allowed_hosts = ["egress-proxy.redwood.internal"] }` to the module inputs. That should satisfy the policy checker.

maya: made the change to use `egress-proxy.redwood.internal` — plan now clean on tags. Running `terraform plan`...

ops-bot: PLAN BLOCKED: freeze-window active; manual exemption required. Ticket created: EX-2026-045 by maya. Add justification and TTL in the ticket to request manual approval.

sam: I'll open the approval thread in #eng-infra-policy and paste the ticket link. Need explicit approver from infra leadership. @jordan can you summarize risk/rollback?

jordan: summarizing: low-risk internal canary, 1 instance NV6 in us-east1, 1-hour TTL, rollback: terraform destroy or scale down to 0, no customer traffic. If quota or network issues arise we'll revert immediately.

lee: I'll monitor quota and netflow during the window. If we see >20% unexpected egress to external CIDRs we'll tear it down.

maya: thanks. Filing final details on EX-2026-045 now. Will wait for manual approval. :hand:

ops-bot: APPROVAL GRANTED BY: infra-lead-smith (manual) — exception EX-2026-045 approved for 1 hour. Please include `exemption_id = "EX-2026-045"` in the PR description for audit.

maya: deploying canary in us-east1 with target_size=1. will post results in 30m.

sam: noted. leave a runbook snippet here for rollback: ```
# rollback
terraform apply -var 'target_size=0' -auto-approve
```

jordan: thanks team. Keep the channel updated if anything weird pops.

maya: will do — initial perf run looks good, latency down ~12% vs baseline. closing once metrics stable. :tada:
